title: Products Never Ordered
description:
Find all products that have **never appeared** in any order. Use a LEFT JOIN between `products` and `order_items`.

**Table: products**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| category | VARCHAR |
| price | DECIMAL |
| stock_quantity | INT |

**Table: order_items**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| order_id | INT |
| product_id | INT |
| quantity | INT |
| unit_price | DECIMAL |

Output columns: `name`, `category`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, stock_quantity INT); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Laptop','Electronics',999.99,10),(2,'Phone','Electronics',699.99,25),(3,'Desk','Furniture',299.99,5),(4,'Chair','Furniture',149.99,8),(5,'Monitor','Electronics',349.99,15); CREATE TABLE order_items (id INT, order_id INT, product_id INT, quantity INT, unit_price DECIMAL); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1,1,1,1,999.99),(2,1,3,2,299.99),(3,2,2,1,699.99);
solution_sql: SELECT p.name, p.category FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.product_id IS NULL ORDER BY p.name

test_cases.description: Chair and Monitor were never ordered

hints: LEFT JOIN keeps all products, even those with no matching order_items row.
When no order_items row matches, oi.product_id will be NULL — filter on that.
explanation: A LEFT JOIN from products to order_items keeps every product. Products 4 (Chair) and 5 (Monitor) have no matching order_items rows, so `oi.product_id IS NULL` for them. That condition isolates never-ordered products.
